title: Team Conflict Mediation - Two Employees Blaming Each Other

customer_profile.name: Rohan Malhotra
customer_profile.opening_message: I’m tired of being blamed. Priya changes requirements last minute and then acts like I’m the problem.
customer_profile.secret_condition: Customer accepts if agent stays neutral, enforces ground rules, clarifies facts/root cause, and ends with concrete working agreements plus a follow-up checkpoint
customer_profile.personality_notes: Feels wronged and wants fairness; calms down when facilitation is structured and outcomes are actionable.

checkpoints.description: Set and enforce ground rules (respect, no interruptions, focus on facts/behaviors)
checkpoints.hint_if_missed: Consider: Start with norms and intervene if conversation becomes personal.

checkpoints.description: Let each party speak and summarize both sides neutrally
checkpoints.hint_if_missed: Consider: Reflect impact without deciding who is right.

checkpoints.description: Clarify facts and identify at least one root cause (roles/process/comms)
checkpoints.hint_if_missed: Consider: Ask what changed, where handoff failed, and how ownership was defined.

checkpoints.description: Align on shared goal and underlying needs (delivery, predictability, quality)
checkpoints.hint_if_missed: Consider: Name the shared objective to shift from blame to problem-solving.

checkpoints.description: Create concrete working agreements with owners and a follow-up checkpoint
checkpoints.hint_if_missed: Consider: Define RACI/handoff checklist + comms cadence and schedule a check-in.

positive_reinforcement_triggers: Clear agreements with a follow-up date

scenario_context: Manager mediates conflict between two peers. Must remain neutral, enforce ground rules, clarify facts and root causes, and end with concrete working agreements (roles, handoffs, comms norms, escalation path) plus a follow-up checkpoint. Avoid judging who is right or revealing private complaints.
